title: 10 Chess Rules Most Players Get Wrong

intro.say: Ten chess rules that most players get wrong. Keep score: for every position, decide your answer before I reveal it. Let's see how many you get right out of ten.
intro.caption: Keep score. Decide before the answer.

segments.say: The king and rook haven't moved, and the king is not in check. Can White castle?
segments.caption: Can White castle here?

segments.say: No. The bishop attacks f1, and the king may never pass through an attacked square. It also can't castle out of check, or into check.
segments.caption: Out of, into or THROUGH check

segments.say: But if only the rook is attacked, castling is completely legal.
segments.caption: Rook attacked = still legal

segments.say: White castles, and the rook escapes at the same time.
segments.caption: Rook attacked = still legal

segments.say: Now the queenside. Black's rook attacks b1, a square White's rook has to cross. Can White castle?
segments.caption: The rook crosses b1...

segments.say: Yes! Only the squares the king walks over matter: e1, d1 and c1. The b1 square doesn't count.
segments.caption: Only the KING's squares count

segments.say: White's king steps to f1, then walks straight back to e1. Nothing has changed. So can White castle now?
segments.caption: Can White castle now?

segments.say: No! Once the king has moved, castling is gone for the rest of the game, even if it walks back.
segments.caption: King moved = castling gone

segments.say: But if only a rook moves away and comes back, you lose castling on that side only.
segments.caption: Rook moved: that side only

segments.say: So White can still castle the other way.
segments.caption: Queenside is still OK

segments.say: Black pushes the pawn two squares and lands right next to White's pawn. Can White capture it?
segments.caption: Can White capture it?

segments.say: Yes! It's called en passant. White captures it as if it had only moved one square.
segments.caption: Capture 'in passing'

segments.say: The catch: you can only do it on the very next move. Wait one move and the chance is gone forever.
segments.caption: Only on the very next move

segments.say: White is a whole queen up and plays queen g6. Black's king has no moves left. Is that a win?
segments.caption: Queen g6. Is it a win?

segments.say: No! Black is not in check, but has no legal move. That's stalemate, and the game is a draw.
segments.caption: No moves + no check = draw

segments.say: Queen g7 instead is checkmate, because now the king is in check.
segments.caption: Qg7 is the win

segments.say: When a pawn reaches the last rank, it can become a queen, rook, bishop or knight. Even a second queen is allowed. But never a king, and it can't stay a pawn.
segments.caption: Any piece. Even a 2nd queen.

segments.say: And sometimes a queen is the wrong choice. Here a queen isn't even check, but a knight is checkmate.
segments.caption: Knight = checkmate

segments.say: Black's queen is hanging on d4, and White's knight attacks it. Can White take the queen?
segments.caption: Can the knight take?

segments.say: No! The knight is pinned. If it moves, the rook attacks the king, and you can never put your own king in check.
segments.caption: Never expose your own king

segments.say: Can White's king walk to e5, right next to Black's king?
segments.caption: Can the king go to e5?

segments.say: Never. Two kings can never stand next to each other, because each one would be in check.
segments.caption: Kings always keep a gap

segments.say: This face-off is called the opposition, and it decides a lot of endgames.
segments.caption: It's called the opposition

segments.say: White has an extra bishop. Can White still win this?
segments.caption: Extra bishop. Can White win?

segments.say: No. King and bishop can't checkmate, so the game is drawn right away. The same goes for king and knight.
segments.caption: King + bishop = draw

segments.say: Two knights are different: mate can't be forced, but it's possible if the defender blunders, so the game goes on.
segments.caption: Two knights: the game goes on

segments.say: White's king is in check from the queen. Can the king simply take it?
segments.caption: Can the king take the queen?

segments.say: Yes! A king can capture any piece that isn't protected.
segments.caption: Unprotected = take it

segments.say: But if a rook protects the queen, taking it would walk into check. The king has to run.
segments.caption: Protected = you can't take

segments.say: Here king f1 is the only legal move.
segments.caption: The only move: Kf1

outro.say: So what's your score out of ten? Write it in the comments, and subscribe for daily chess rules, traps and puzzles.
outro.caption: Comment your score out of 10!
